Thereafter the court of Sessions, upon compliance of the direction of the High Court Division, allowed cross-examination and then having retried the case taking Vs. The State Tat hlam,1) 103 evidence afresh by judgment and order dated '17.1.1.1992 convicted the appellant under Section 302 of the Penal Code and also convicted Imam. Hossain under section 302/109 of the Penal Code and sentenced both of them to imprisonment for idle and a fine of Tk.5000/-. Then the appellant and Imam Hossain filed the present. Criminal Appeal No.682 of 1983 and the High Court Division dismissed the appeal of the appellant and allowed the appeal of Imam Hossain. 

 3. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that if the examination-in-chief as well as cross-examination of the eye witnesses i.e. P.W.s. 2,4, 5 and 6 are put in juxtaposition then it would be clear that their evidence is most unworthy of credit to justify the order of conviction of the appellant and there are serious contradictions in the evidence of eye witnesses that is P.W.2A5 and 6 and the prosecution failed to prove its case with regard to the infliction of dagger blow by the appellant on the body of the victim as such the order of conviction against the appellant is liable to be set aside. The learned counsel for respondent submits that contradictions and omissions are not vital so as to set aside the conviction of the appellant. 

 Sections 302/109 of the Penal Code upon observing than "we noticed .that P.Ws. 2-6 did not state in corroboration with each other consistently as to utter or use of any common words of language by accused Imam Hossain while giving alleged order to accused Abul Khair to go for action, rather the evidence in cross-examination of P.Ws.26 during retrial on second occasion they stated that different words by accused Imam Hossain in alleged order to accused Abul Khair. In the light of above decision above in the words or language used by accused Imam Hossain, in view of evidence of P.Ws. 2-6 during retrial on second occasion, accused Imam Hossain can have no liability for offence under section 302/109 of the Penal Code and in the above context trial court had no reliable legal evidence to find accused Imam Hossain liable for offence under section 302/109 of the Penal Code in order to be convicted and sentenced thereunder 

 5. It also appears that the High Court Division dismissed the appeal of the appellant upon observing that (.1) P. Ws. 2-6 being resent on the spot during occurrence duly recognized the appellant with light of moon which was shining at that night in the sky and (2) P.Ws.2-6 stated clearly that they saw and recognized the appellant as the assailant and that they had no difficulty to recognize the appellant "with the light of moon" and (3) there is nothing in the evidence of P.Ws.2-6 to discard their evidence relating to recognition of the appellant during. occurrence. But as it appears the High Court Division at the same time observed that P.Ws. 2, 4, 5 and 6. contradicted each other to the extent that P.W.2 stated that the appellant was facing north when he gave dagger blow in the chest of deceased Julfu Master and the appellant was wearing a coloured shirt and Imam Hossain (since acquitted) was wearing a Panjabi, P.W.5 stated that the appellant was facing west at the time of inflicting injury and the appellant was wearing a genji and accused Imam Hossain had no wearing at that time and P.W.6 stated that the appellant was facing south at the time of inflicting of blow by dagger and the appellant and Imam 

 Hossain had no wearing and so we are of the view that the conviction of the appellant is unwarranted as the basic principles of criminal jurisprudence is that the prosecution has to prove. its case beyond reasonable doubt. Moreover the above irreconcilable contradictions mean that the P.Ws. did not see the occurrence at all. Under the fundamental scheme of criminal jurisprudence discrepancies, contradictions and omissions in the evidence of eye witnesses are.to be taken into consideration otherwise error might creep up in the judgment resulting in the conviction of the accused. So in view of the above and that lmam Hossain has been acquitted we are of the' view that the appellant is entitled to the benefit of doubt.
